terra.problem: “Paul hands the whole job to God” suggests God is doing the imitating. Paul tells the believers to imitate God.
The explanation repeats that the verse is certain and clear without adding much explanation or Papa Dorin’s personality.
The explanation simply identifies the parenthetical note and says it is easy to miss. It is flat and generic.
The explanation repeats the location and wording of the note, then offers a generic observation about missing it.
“Empty words sound nice” adds a description Paul does not give.
The closing line makes a joke about how the line of Scripture is written.
“That’s a lot of work for one verse” makes the verse itself the subject of a joke.
“The sleeper wakes up, rises” presents the saying’s commands as actions the sleeper actually takes. The text does not say that happens.
The closing line comments on the choices in the blank, drawing attention to the lesson’s own question.
“Wine is the thing to leave alone” goes beyond Paul’s instruction not to get drunk on wine.
